findings.description:
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses logical AND instead of OR, preventing team admins and owners from adding guests. — WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses the `&&` operator instead of `||` to combine `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`.
WHY: Because a team member cannot be both an admin and an owner at the same time, this condition will always evaluate to `false`, wrongly throwing a `FORBIDDEN` error when a team admin or owner tries to add guests.
HOW: Replace `&&` with `||` so the check succeeds if the user is either a team admin or a team owner.

Calling .scrub on i.content without checking for nil causes NoMethodError on RSS feeds that only provide description tags. — WHAT: `i.content.scrub` is called on SimpleRSS items without a fallback or nil guard.
WHY: In standard RSS 2.0 feeds, post bodies are often placed in `<description>` rather than `<content>`, causing `i.content` to be `nil` and raising `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`, crashing the feed poll job.
HOW: Fall back to `i.description` if `i.content` is blank and guard against `nil` before calling `scrub` and `CGI.unescapeHTML`.

Missing require 'open-uri' in TopicEmbed causes open(url) to treat HTTP URLs as local filenames and fail. — WHAT: `open(url)` is used to fetch remote web pages in `import_remote` without requiring `open-uri`.
WHY: When `import_remote` is called directly (such as via `TopicRetriever` before `Jobs::PollFeed` runs), `Kernel#open` is not monkey-patched by `open-uri` and attempts to open the URL as a local file path, raising `Errno::ENOENT`.
HOW: Add `require 'open-uri'` before calling `open(url)`.

Device ID is cached in localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, causing subsequent requests from rejected devices to bypass the device limit. — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key in `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` executes and succeeds.
WHY: When `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (or a database error), the error is returned to `Authenticate` and the request is rejected once, but the device key remains in `localCache` for 29 minutes; subsequent requests with the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` will hit the cache, return `nil`, and allow unauthorized anonymous access past the device limit.
HOW: Move `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` to only run after `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device)` completes without error.

Device key is stored in localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, causing subsequent requests from rejected devices to bypass the device limit. — WHAT: `tagDeviceUI` populates `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds, leaving the device ID cached when `CreateOrUpdateDevice` fails with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.
WHY: A device that exceeds the limit is rejected on its first request, but subsequent requests within the 29-minute cache window hit `localCache.Get` and return `nil`, bypassing the device limit entirely.
HOW: Update `tagDeviceUI` to set the key in `localCache` only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or remove the key from `localCache` if `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns an error).

DualWriterMode3.Create records legacy storage duration metric instead of storage duration metric when storage create fails — WHAT: `d.Storage.Create` failure invokes `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Skews legacy metrics with failures and durations originating from the unified storage operation.
HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration` with `d.recordStorageDuration`.

DualWriterMode3.Delete uses wrong context logger and passes resource name instead of kind to recordStorageDuration — WHAT: `DualWriterMode3.Delete` attaches `d.Log` instead of `log` to the context and passes `name` instead of `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Context logger loses the decorated structured fields (`name`, `kind`, `method`), and Prometheus metrics record high-cardinality resource names in the `kind` metric label dimension.
HOW: Pass `log` to `klog.NewContext` and `options.Kind` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

DualWriterMode3.Update records legacy storage duration metric instead of storage duration metric when storage update fails — WHAT: `d.Storage.Update` failure calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Incorrectly attributes unified store update errors and latency to the legacy store metric stream.
HOW: Call `d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`.

DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection records storage duration instead of legacy duration for legacy delete operation — WHAT: In the asynchronous goroutine for legacy `DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.
WHY: Legacy delete collection metrics are recorded into the unified store duration metric collector rather than the legacy store metric collector.
HOW: Change `d.recordStorageDuration` to `d.recordLegacyDuration`.

Record storage duration instead of legacy duration when Storage.Create fails — WHAT: `d.Storage.Create` failure invokes `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Incorrectly records unified store failures and latencies against legacy store metrics, distorting observability and alerts.
HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration` with `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Use contextual logger in Delete context and pass options.Kind to recordStorageDuration — WHAT: `DualWriterMode3.Delete` attaches `d.Log` instead of `log` to the context and passes `name` instead of `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Downstream storage calls lose contextual logger values (`name`, `kind`, `method`) and Prometheus metrics record the resource instance name under the `kind` metric label, creating cardinality explosion.
HOW: Pass `log` to `klog.NewContext` and `options.Kind` to `d.recordStorageDuration`.

Record storage duration instead of legacy duration when Storage.Update fails — WHAT: `d.Storage.Update` failure calls `d.recordLegacyDuration` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`.
WHY: Incorrectly attributes unified store update errors and latency to legacy store metrics.
HOW: Call `d.recordStorageDuration` with `options.Kind` on unified storage error.

Record legacy duration instead of storage duration for async Legacy.DeleteCollection — WHAT: In the asynchronous goroutine for legacy `DeleteCollection`, `d.recordStorageDuration` is called instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`.
WHY: Asynchronous legacy delete-collection operations report duration and error status to the unified storage metric series instead of the legacy metric series.
HOW: Call `d.recordLegacyDuration` inside the legacy cleanup goroutine.

Calling sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source raises TypeError because integration implementations do not accept this argument. — WHAT: `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` is invoked with the unexpected keyword argument `assignment_source`.
WHY: `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` and its concrete subclasses (`JiraIntegration`, `VstsIntegration`, `ExampleIntegration`) only accept `(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `**kwargs` or `assignment_source`, which causes a `TypeError` and crashes the outbound sync task whenever assignee sync runs.
HOW: Either remove `assignment_source` from the call to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound` (since `should_sync` already performs the source check) or update the `sync_assignee_outbound` method signatures on `IssueSyncIntegration` and all integration subclasses to accept `assignment_source=None, **kwargs`.

Default value for queued is evaluated at module import time instead of instantiation time. — WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at module import time rather than at dataclass instantiation.
WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` instance created using the default value receives the fixed timestamp from when the module was loaded rather than the current time when the assignment was queued.
HOW: Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so that `timezone.now()` is called afresh each time an instance is instantiated.

Duplicate method definition for `downsize` overwrites the multi-argument version and breaks existing callers. — WHAT: Defining `self.downsize` twice in succession overwrites the first definition with `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`.
WHY: Callers expecting the 4/5 argument signature (such as `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) will fail with an `ArgumentError` or `TypeError` at runtime.
HOW: Combine both argument styles into a single method that checks the types of the parameters and formats `dimensions` accordingly.
